summary: Tirofiban is an IV reversible GP IIb/IIIa receptor antagonist used in non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS) to reduce thrombotic cardiovascular events. Given as 25 mcg/kg over 5 minutes then 0.15 mcg/kg/min for up to 18 hours, with the maintenance infusion halved to 0.075 mcg/kg/min when CrCl <=60 mL/min. Bleeding and thrombocytopenia are the key risks.
indications: Reduce the rate of thrombotic cardiovascular events (combined endpoint of death, myocardial infarction, or refractory ischemia/repeat cardiac procedure) in patients with non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS)

dosage.d: 25 mcg/kg IV within 5 minutes, then 0.15 mcg/kg/min infusion
dosage.t: Bolus then continuous infusion for up to 18 hours
dosage.n: Administered with aspirin and an anticoagulant (heparin or bivalirudin)

dosage.d: 25 mcg/kg IV within 5 minutes, then 0.075 mcg/kg/min infusion
dosage.t: Bolus then continuous infusion for up to 18 hours
dosage.n: CrCl by Cockcroft-Gault using actual body weight; halved maintenance rate

admin: For intravenous use only; do not give by any other route
May be administered from the 250 mL premixed bag (50 mcg/mL); do NOT dilute
Give the bolus dose within 5 minutes via IV pump, then immediately start the maintenance infusion via IV pump
Inspect visually for particulate matter/discoloration; do not use unless clear and seal intact; discard unused portion in bag

Compatible in the same line with heparin, atropine, dobutamine, dopamine, epinephrine, famotidine, furosemide, lidocaine, midazolam, morphine, nitroglycerin, potassium chloride, propranolol; do NOT give in the same line as diazepam
Minimize arterial/venous punctures, IM injections, nasotracheal intubation and other traumatic procedures to reduce bleeding
moa: Tirofiban is a reversible non-peptide antagonist of fibrinogen binding to the platelet glycoprotein (GP) IIb/IIIa receptor, the major surface receptor mediating platelet aggregation. By blocking this final common pathway it inhibits platelet aggregation in a dose- and concentration-dependent manner, achieving >90% inhibition within about 10 minutes of the recommended bolus; the effect reverses 4 to 8 hours after the infusion stops.

absolute: History of thrombocytopenia following prior tirofiban exposure
History of bleeding diathesis, major surgical procedure or severe physical trauma within the previous month
relative: Concomitant fibrinolytics, anticoagulants or other antiplatelet agents (additive bleeding)
Prior exposure to a GP IIb/IIIa receptor antagonist (thrombocytopenia risk)
Elderly with higher baseline bleeding risk
monitor: Severe renal insufficiency (reduce dose; not studied in hemodialysis)

preg: Available case reports have not established an association with major birth defects, miscarriage or adverse maternal/fetal outcomes, though data cannot definitively establish absence of risk. Animal studies up to 5 mg/kg/day showed no fetal harm. Untreated myocardial infarction is a medical emergency that can be fatal to mother and fetus.
lact: No data on presence in human milk, effects on the breastfed infant, or on milk production; tirofiban is present in rat milk. Weigh the developmental/health benefits of breastfeeding against the mother's clinical need and potential infant risk.
renal: Patients with moderate-to-severe renal insufficiency have decreased plasma clearance. For CrCl <=60 mL/min reduce the maintenance infusion to 0.075 mcg/kg/min (bolus unchanged). Plasma clearance falls ~40% with CrCl <60 mL/min and >50% with CrCl <30 mL/min. Tirofiban is removed by hemodialysis; safety/efficacy in dialysis patients not established.
hepatic: No effect of hepatic impairment on tirofiban clearance; no dosage adjustment is recommended for hepatic impairment.

major: Fibrinolytics (e.g., alteplase) - markedly increased bleeding risk
Anticoagulants (heparin, warfarin, DOACs) - increased bleeding risk
Other antiplatelet agents (aspirin, clopidogrel) - increased bleeding risk (used together intentionally with monitoring)
moderate: Drugs affecting hemostasis (e.g., NSAIDs) - additive bleeding risk
minor: None of clinical significance identified in labeling
interactions.food: Not applicable; administered intravenously in an acute care setting.
interactions.alcohol: Not relevant during acute parenteral therapy.
interactions.diagnostics: Prolongs bleeding time; may lower platelet count and hemoglobin/hematocrit.

common: Bleeding (most common; often at the arterial access site)

monitoring: Platelet count at baseline, about 6 hours after initiation, and daily thereafter
Hemoglobin and hematocrit; signs and symptoms of bleeding
Arterial access site and puncture sites for hematoma/bleeding
Renal function (CrCl) to confirm correct infusion rate
If platelets fall <90,000/mm3, exclude pseudothrombocytopenia; if confirmed, discontinue tirofiban and heparin
counsel: This medicine is given through a vein in the hospital to help prevent blood clots in your heart vessels
Report any unusual bleeding, bruising, blood in urine or stool, or black tarry stools immediately
Tell staff about any recent surgery, trauma, ulcers, or bleeding problems
Bed rest and gentle handling of access sites may be required to limit bleeding
Report any rash, swelling, difficulty breathing, or signs of allergic reaction
pk: >90% platelet inhibition within ~10 minutes of bolus
Effect reaches maximum during/just after bolus
Platelet function returns toward baseline in 4-8 hours after stopping
Store premixed bag at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light/freezing per label
pearls: Reversible GP IIb/IIIa inhibitor: platelet function recovers within hours of stopping the infusion
Halve the maintenance infusion (to 0.075 mcg/kg/min) when CrCl <=60 mL/min - the bolus is unchanged
Cleared largely by the kidney and removed by hemodialysis, unlike most highly protein-bound drugs
Check platelets ~6 hours in to catch acute profound thrombocytopenia early
Most bleeding occurs at the femoral arterial access site after catheterization
missed: Administered by a clinician as a continuous IV infusion; not self-dosed. Infusion rate is managed and adjusted by the care team, and the drug is stopped if uncontrolled bleeding occurs.
overdose: The most frequent manifestation of overdose is bleeding, primarily minor mucocutaneous and access-site bleeding. Treat by assessing clinical status and stopping or reducing the infusion as appropriate. Tirofiban can be removed by hemodialysis.
